originalRequest: Based on this current website improve the overall design while keeping the same content. I want to preserve the topographic lines theme but I also want the website to run well on mobiles , 4K screens or lower end pcs. The end result shouldn't be too fancy as it's a website for a gameplay programmer portfolio, not a web developer
subject: Personal portfolio of Marco Piamonte, a gameplay programmer based in Malmö, Sweden (from Italy), studying Game Programming
pageType: Existing multi-page static portfolio site redesign (index.html home plus project detail pages and resume.html)
scope: Visual redesign of the existing site keeping all current content: home page (hero, about, projects grid, contact) as the primary focus, with consistent styling carried to the project detail pages (castlebound, gunsmoke, photon-dash, playfab, slimyfiles, steelsilk, zombie) and resume page. No new content sections or invented content.
primaryGoal: Present Marco's gameplay programming work clearly to recruiters and studios so they browse projects and get in touch, with a cleaner, more polished look that performs well on every device
audience: Game studio recruiters, hiring leads and fellow developers reviewing gameplay programmer candidates, on desktop (including 4K), laptops, low-end PCs and mobile
offer: A gameplay programmer with shipped and prototype projects in Unreal and Unity (C++, C#), including gameplay and network programming work
primaryAction: Open project pages and view the resume, then contact via the contact form or Git/LinkedIn/Itch links
creativeControl: Designer may refine layout, spacing, typography hierarchy, color usage and card styling, but must keep all content, the topographic theme and a modest, performance-first aesthetic
requiredContent: Navigation: logo name 'Marco Piamonte', links Home, About Me, Projects, Contact, Resume, hamburger on mobile, GitHub/LinkedIn/Itch icon buttons
Hero: 'Marco Piamonte', 'Gameplay Programmer', '📍Malmö, Sweden', tool/skill icons (Unreal, Unity, C++, C#, Git, Subversion, Perforce, Rider) over the animated topographic line canvas
About: profile photo (Media/ProfilePic.jpg) and existing bio text unchanged

Projects: cards for Castlebound, Gunsmoke and Grimoires, Photon Dash, Slimy Files, Steelsilk Championship, Zombie FPS, MatchMaking Project (PlayFab), each with its existing screenshot from Media/Projects, status/date/role line (e.g. 'Published, 14th March 2025, Gameplay Programmer') and link to its detail page
Contact Me: existing form with Email, Subject, Message fields
Project detail pages and resume page: same content, restyled to match the home page (resume links MarcoPiamonte_CV.pdf)
constraints: Keep all existing content and copy; only improve design and presentation
Preserve the topographic contour-lines theme (bg.js Perlin-noise marching-squares canvas)

Must perform well on mobile, 4K displays and low-end PCs: keep adaptive resolution, cap DPR/resolution on 4K, static or reduced render on mobile, pause when offscreen/hidden, honor prefers-reduced-motion
Restrained, not flashy: a gameplay programmer portfolio, not a web-dev showcase; avoid heavy effects, glassmorphism stacks, large libraries
Static HTML/CSS/vanilla JS site (no framework); keep existing file structure and assets
Responsive layout scaling cleanly from small phones to 4K (fluid type, max content width)
Hide the FPS counter (showFPS currently true) in production
Subtle entrance/scroll animations allowed, lightweight and disabled under prefers-reduced-motion
brandInputs: Colors: primary blue #1723cc (most used), accents rgb(106,114,230), rgb(90,99,220), violet #380bbf, dark greys rgba(36,36,36), #0f172a, highlight #fff700 (style.css)
Visual style: dark background with animated topographic contour lines canvas (bg.js), card-based sections
Assets: Media/ProfilePic.jpg, project screenshots in Media/Projects, tool icons and social icons in Media
assumptions: Home page is the main focus; detail and resume pages get the same visual system for consistency
Section count stays as existing (hero, about, projects, contact) rather than expanding to eight, since the user asked to keep the same content
Existing blue/violet palette and Poppins/Nunito are kept as a starting point but may be refined for contrast
Typo fixes in dates (e.g. 'Februrary', '22th') are left as content unless the build phase treats them as minor copy corrections
Light entrance and scroll animations are kept, respecting reduced-motion
unresolved: Whether the contact form has a working backend (main.js) is unverified; keep current behavior
